paragraphs: Aylesbury is the county town of Buckinghamshire, and children in care from the town are looked after by Buckinghamshire Council's own fostering service and by the agencies shown above. The council says it has more than 500 children in its care, and it is looking in particular for homes for brothers and sisters, older children and teenagers, children with complex needs and children from minority ethnic groups.

Much of the council's fostering life happens in Aylesbury. It runs support groups for carers in Aylesbury as well as in north and south Bucks, some in the daytime and some in the evening, in person and online, alongside a buddy scheme, holiday groups for carers' own sons and daughters and an annual awards evening. It is also setting up Mockingbird groups of foster families in the north, south and centre of the county. Its yearly carers' conference in May 2025 was held in Aylesbury, and that spring it ran fostering stalls at Aylesbury Market and The Gateway.

In 2024 the council introduced a package of benefits for its own carers, including help with council tax for carers with a placement for at least 182 days of the year, free parking in council car parks, free bus travel for carers and the children they look after, and leisure centre membership. In 2025 it added further perks, among them help towards holidays and discounted rail travel. Its corporate parenting strategy for 2025 to 2030 aims to keep more children living within Buckinghamshire, close to their schools and friends.

The council's next online information session is on 9 December 2026. Our Buckinghamshire page covers the whole county, and our Milton Keynes and Oxfordshire pages cover the neighbouring areas. Talk to the council and to two or three of the services above before you decide.
